Quick update from Product/Research:
- Baseline: with the current LLM config (redwood-catalyst-7B, 16-token avg), lab p95 is ~55ms on an A100 equivalent under our microbench harness. In production we typically see a +20–30ms delta depending on KV cache warm state and sequence length.
- Recommendation: to hit the requested p95 < 60ms in a real pilot, we should:
  1) provision a warm dedicated pool (reserved instances) for their scheduled windows, with prefix caching enabled;
  2) pin to the 6B quantized variant for the high-throughput windows (drop in avg latency, small quality delta);
  3) set a soft concurrency cap per-worker to limit noisy-neighbor effects and favor tail reduction.

Operational implications and rough cost uplift (ballpark): +25–40% on token compute for the scheduled windows given reserved capacity and fewer multiplexing efficiencies. There are also engineering work items: a short QA verification harness for sequence length distributions, and a monitoring dashboard for the endpoint (we can base on existing per-route tracing).

I can assemble the verification plan (what metrics to collect, sample size, acceptance tests) if Sean can confirm Ops feasibility for warm pools and runbook items.

— Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime

Agree with Marcus — ops can support but need procurement signoff on the cost uplift and a few guardrails:
- We require a one-week warm-up window before the pilot start to populate KV caches and stress the warm pool;
- We’ll schedule two supervised test windows (30–60 minutes) to validate the telemetry before going live;
- If observed p95 exceeds 80ms during the pilot, we automatically switch to the fallback model (quantized high-availability variant) and inform the NexusCare SPOC within 10 minutes.

I’ll estimate the precise capacity delta and provide an ops runbook draft by EOD today. Also flagging that Legal may want a short clause about measurement methodology (how p95 is computed, sampling, timezone of agreed windows).
